title: Value of a Function at a Point
notes: **Direct substitution.** When a lies in the domain and the formula is continuous there, f(a) is found by replacing x with a; for f(x) = x² + 3x, f(2) = 4 + 6 = 10.
**Limit versus value.** lim(x→a) f(x) uses values NEAR a, while f(a) uses only the value AT a; the two may differ or the latter may not exist at all.
**Removable hole.** For f(x) = (x² − 4)/(x − 2), f(2) is undefined but lim(x→2) f(x) = 4, because the expression equals x + 2 for every x ≠ 2.
**Redefinition.** Defining f(2) = 4 fills the hole and makes f continuous at 2; defining f(2) = 7 keeps the same limit but leaves a removable discontinuity.
**Piecewise boundaries.** At a point where the rule changes, f(a) belongs to exactly one branch (usually the one with ≤ or ≥); read the inequality before substituting.
**Exam caution.** Substituting first into a 0/0 form gives no information; always simplify the expression before evaluating at the point.
summary: f(a) is obtained by direct substitution; the limit as x approaches a is independent of f(a) and can exist even when f(a) is undefined.
